title: Framework for Integrating Machine Learning Methods for Path-Aware Source Routing
problem: Traffic engineering in SDN requires complex optimal flow allocation and routing decisions to minimize congestion, but creating optimized solutions is cumbersome as traffic patterns vary with network scale and capacity.
motivation: Machine learning methods can find optimized traffic engineering solutions to improve network performance by adapting to dynamic traffic patterns.
method: The framework integrates Hecate, which applies deep reinforcement learning and classification to compute optimal paths from real-time traffic statistics, with PolKA source routing tool to dynamically allocate flows. The system is validated on a real network using P4 testbed emulation to demonstrate practical ML-driven path optimization.
key_novelty: Practical integration of ML-based traffic engineering (Hecate) with source routing (PolKA) on real networks, bridging theoretical TE methods to operational self-driving network deployment.
contributions: Framework combining Hecate ML-based TE with PolKA source routing for practical real-network implementation
Demonstration of ML-driven path computation using real-time traffic statistics on emulated P4 testbed
Practical methodology for dynamic flow allocation through ML-optimized paths and source routing control
Proof-of-concept translating theoretical traffic engineering approaches to practice
primary_theme: ML-driven network traffic engineering via source routing
